Web radios of the whole world in Gladys, from
[Radio Browser](https://www.radio-browser.info/), a free directory of about
50,000 stations run by volunteers. This integration is not affiliated with
radio-browser.info.

## What it does

- **Search** the directory by name, country, language or genre, from the
  Configuration tab of the integration.
- **Keep your favorite stations**: each favorite becomes a device in Gladys,
  with its stream state, bitrate, codec and stream address.
- **Show them on the dashboard** with their logo, in the **Favorite radios**
  widget.
- **Use them in scenes**: the **Get the stream of a radio** and **Pick a
  random radio** scene actions hand the stream address to the player of your
  choice (for example the DLNA integration).

Gladys cannot yet let an integration start the player of another
integration: playing a radio therefore takes two actions in a scene (see
[Scene examples](#scene-examples)).

## Before you start

- Gladys 5.1.0 or later.
- Internet access from the machine running Gladys. No account, no key.
- To listen to a radio: an integration whose player can play a URL in a
  scene, such as the **DLNA** integration ("Play a URL on a DLNA renderer"
  action).

## Configuration

Open the **Configuration** tab of the integration.

- **Language of names and messages**: the language of the feature names of
  the stations you add from now on (Gladys keeps them once a device is
  added), and of the error messages of the scene actions. French by default.
- **Refresh interval (minutes)**: how often the favorites are read again from
  Radio Browser, 60 minutes by default (15 to 360).

### Finding and adding stations

The favorites are managed with the actions at the bottom of the
Configuration tab (click **Run** under each one):

1. **Search a station**: fill in one field or more, for example the name
   `FIP`, or the genre `jazz` and the country `FR`. The country is a name in
   English (`France`, `Germany`) or a two-letter code; the language is
   written in English (`french`, `german`). The 10 most played working
   stations are listed, each with a number. Stations already in your
   favorites carry a ★.
2. **Add to favorites**: type the number of a result of the last search (or
   the identifier, UUID, of a station, or its radio-browser.info address).
   You may give it another name. Up to 50 favorites.
3. Open the **Discover** tab: the station is there. Click **Add to Gladys**.
4. **List the favorites** shows them, numbered, and whether they were added
   to Gladys.
5. **Remove a favorite** takes its number in that list, its name or its
   UUID. Its device stays in Gladys: delete it from the **Devices** tab if
   you no longer want it.

The favorites are stored in the integration's data folder, with their last
known details: the dashboard and the scenes keep working when the directory
is down.

## The station devices

Each favorite added to Gladys is a device named after the station, with four
read-only features:

| Feature        | What it says                                                                                                          |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Stream online  | On when the last check of the stream by Radio Browser succeeded, Off when it failed or the station left the directory |
| Bitrate        | In kbit/s, as announced by the station (not sent when unknown)                                                        |
| Codec          | MP3, AAC, OGG...                                                                                                      |
| Stream address | The address to give to a player                                                                                       |

The country, language, genres, website and logo address are kept as device
parameters. The device is refreshed by the integration itself, at the
interval of the configuration.

## The "Favorite radios" widget

Add the **Favorite radios** widget to a dashboard. It shows your favorites
with their logo, country, codec and bitrate, and a green **Online** or red
**Offline** badge. Tap a station to see its language, its genres, and links to
its website and, when the stream is secure (https), to the stream itself:
your browser plays it in a new tab.

Settings:

- **Stations shown**: pick some of the stations added to Gladys, in the order
  you want; empty shows every favorite (12 at most).
- **Display**: a **Logo grid**, or a **List (8 at most)**.

The widget has no "play" button: Gladys does not let an integration start
the player of another integration yet.

## Scene triggers and actions

The integration declares no scene trigger: a station going offline is the
state of its **Stream online** feature, which the "Device state changed"
trigger of Gladys already covers.

### Get the stream of a radio

Pick a favorite station. The action gives the following actions of the
scene:

- **Stream address**: to give to the "Play a URL" action of a player;
- **Station name**, **Codec**, **Bitrate (kbit/s)**;
- **Stream online**: the last check of the stream by Radio Browser
  succeeded;
- **HLS stream (.m3u8)**: many network players cannot play those.

It also counts a listen in Radio Browser, as the directory asks. When the
directory does not answer, the last known stream address is given anyway.

### Pick a random radio

A random working station of a **Genre**, a **Country** and/or a **Language**
(same rules as the search). It gives the same values as above.

In the scene editor, the values of an action appear in the variable picker of
the next actions, as `{{0.0.stream_url}}` for the first action of the first
block.

## Scene examples

**Wake up with FIP** (with the DLNA integration):

1. Trigger: **Time**, 7:00, Monday to Friday.
2. Action: **Get the stream of a radio**, station **FIP**.
3. Next block, action: **Play a URL on a DLNA renderer**, renderer of the
   bedroom, URL `{{0.0.stream_url}}`, title `{{0.0.name}}`, volume 20.

**A random jazz radio on Sunday morning**:

1. Trigger: **Time**, 10:00, Sunday.
2. Action: **Pick a random radio**, genre `jazz`.
3. Next block, action: **Play a URL on a DLNA renderer**, URL
   `{{0.0.stream_url}}`, title `{{0.0.name}}`.

**Be told when your favorite station is down**:

1. Trigger: **Device state changed**, feature **Stream online** of the
   station, equal to 0.
2. Action: **Send a message**: "FIP is offline in Radio Browser".

## Troubleshooting

- **"Radio Browser cannot be reached"** in the Configuration tab: check that
  the Gladys machine has Internet access. The directory runs on servers
  maintained by volunteers: the integration tries the next server, and again
  at the next refresh. The favorites keep their last known details meanwhile.
- **A station is offline but plays**: the state is the directory's last
  check of the stream, which runs about once a day. It follows at the next
  refresh after a new check.
- **No logo**: only PNG, JPEG and WebP logos of 300 KB at most can be shown
  in a Gladys widget; many stations publish an icon (.ico) or an SVG file.
- **The player does not play the stream**: try another version of the
  station (an MP3 one rather than AAC, or http rather than https), and avoid
  HLS streams (.m3u8).
- **The station is not in the Discover tab**: run **List the favorites**,
  then reopen the Discover tab.
- Detailed logs: set the `LOG_LEVEL` variable to `debug`. The logs never
  contain the stream addresses.

## How the integration uses Radio Browser

Radio Browser is free and run by volunteers. The integration follows its
guidelines:

- **one request for all your favorites** at each refresh (every 60 minutes by
  default, 15 minutes at the fastest); a search only when you run it;
- a server picked at random among the ones the directory announces (DNS),
  then the next one when it fails;
- an explicit `User-Agent`: `gladys-radio-browser/<version>`;
- the stream address resolved by the directory (`url_resolved`);
- **a listen counted** each time a scene action starts a station, which keeps
  the popularity of the stations meaningful (the directory counts one per
  day and per address).

Radio Browser publishes no quota. The logos are downloaded directly from the
stations' websites, which then see the Internet address of your home.

## Limits

- **No direct play**: Gladys 5.2 has no way for an integration to command a
  device of another integration, nor a scene action that plays an address on
  the speakers of the core (Sonos, AirPlay, Google Cast: their "play a
  notification" only plays a spoken text, and stops after a few seconds or
  minutes). The stream address goes through a scene to the player of an
  integration that accepts one, like DLNA.
- 50 favorites at most; the widget shows 12 of them (8 as a list).
- The stream state is the one checked by the directory, not a live check.
- Feature names stay in the language they were added in.
- Removing a favorite does not delete its device.
- Developed without a live connection to the directory, on recorded answers
  of its API: feedback welcome on the
  [GitHub repository](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-radio-browser/issues).

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Radio Browser asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | Radio Browser is a free directory of about 50,000 web radios, run by volunteers: no account, no key. Find a station with the "Search a station" action below, then add it with "Add to favorites" and its number. Each favorite then appears in the Discover tab: click "Add to Gladys". This integration is not affiliated with radio-browser.info. |
| Playing a radio | `section` | No | Gladys does not let an integration start the player of another integration yet. In a scene, add the "Get the stream of a radio" action, then the "Play a URL" action of your player (the DLNA integration, for example) with the stream address as URL. The documentation shows a full example. |
| Language of names and messages | `select` | No | Names of the features of the stations added from now on (Gladys keeps them once a device is added), and error messages of the scene actions. |
| Refresh interval (minutes) | `number` | No | How often the favorites are read again from Radio Browser (stream check, bitrate, logo), in one request for all of them. 15 to 360 minutes: the directory checks each stream about once a day. |

## How to install Radio Browser in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Radio Browser appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-radio-browser:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-radio-browser](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-radio-browser).

Radio Browser requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Radio Browser is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core.
